what_was_wrong.summary: OwnedSkey::drop skipped the provider's mandatory free when keydata was NULL. The guard was introduced by 4a088a9fb on the stated premise that the authority's EVP_SKEY_free guards keydata != NULL. That premise is false: the authority calls evp_skeymgmt_freedata unconditionally, and the failure arms of EVP_SKEY_import and EVP_SKEY_generate reach it with keydata == NULL.
what_was_wrong.pre_fix_behaviour: src/evp/skeymgmt.rs OwnedSkey::drop (pre-fix ~:338-340) wrapped the call in `if !(*p).keydata.is_null()`, so the provider free was not called on a failed import/generate.
what_was_wrong.authority_behaviour: EVP_SKEY_free(skey) down-references, then calls evp_skeymgmt_freedata(skey->skeymgmt, skey->keydata) with no key-data test, then EVP_SKEYMGMT_free, CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free and OPENSSL_free. evp_skeymgmt_freedata calls skeymgmt->free(keydata) unconditionally because the slot is mandatory. EVP_SKEY_import's `err:` label and EVP_SKEY_generate's `err:` label both call EVP_SKEY_free before any keydata was assigned.

provider_free_audit.question: Is the candidate's own OSSL_FUNC_skeymgmt_free implementation NULL-safe before the unconditional call is restored?
found: src/provider/skeymgmt.rs:generic_free is the only provider skeymgmt free implementation. It is installed in both the AES table (src/provider/skeymgmt.rs:358-362) and the GENERIC-SECRET table (:333-337), and src/provider/legacyprov.rs reuses GENERIC_SKEYMGMT_FUNCTIONS for the legacy provider.

There is no Box::from_raw and no NonNull::new_unchecked in the free path. generic_free delegates to OwnedCtx::<ProvSkey>::from_raw, which maps NULL to None (src/runtime/bio/owned.rs:180-205); drop(None) is a no-op. The free was therefore already NULL-safe.
changed: src/provider/skeymgmt.rs:148-160 now writes the authority's own first line explicitly (`if keydata.is_null() { return; }`) so the NULL tolerance is visible at the dispatch boundary rather than inferred from OwnedCtx::from_raw.
src/provider/skeymgmt.rs:413-429 adds provider::skeymgmt::tests::the_builtin_provider_free_tolerates_null, which calls generic_free(NULL) under the normal library suite.
provider_free_audit.why_ub_safe: The NULL argument is rejected before any dereference, cast-to-reference or adoption. For a non-NULL key the existing OwnedCtx path releases the secret member with CRYPTO_clear_free and then the block; it does not free the enclosing allocation twice.

the_change.change: Removed the `if !(*p).keydata.is_null()` guard and call evp_skeymgmt_freedata((*p).skeymgmt, (*p).keydata) unconditionally on the last release, restoring the authority's order and call.
Widened the # Safety contracts to `keydata` is NULL or a live provider key produced by this skeymgmt, and recorded that NULL is part of the authority's call contract on the failure arms.
Inverted and renamed the test to a_failed_key_without_data_still_calls_the_provider_destructor_with_null; it now asserts the free count is 1 and the pointer observed by the provider is NULL.
Explicit NULL guard plus the NULL-tolerance test, as recorded in provider_free_audit.

supersedes.false_statement: The authority's EVP_SKEY_free guards keydata != NULL. The import/generate failure paths free a key whose keydata was never produced, so a mandatory provider free(NULL) was invoked in a state the authority never invokes.
supersedes.correction: The authority has no such guard at s_lib.c:207-226 and does invoke the mandatory free with NULL on exactly those failure paths.

supersedes.false_statement: Restored the authority's keydata != NULL guard in Drop.
supersedes.correction: There was no authority guard to restore. The guard has been removed and the unconditional call restored.

supersedes.false_statement: The provider free callback is no longer invoked with NULL key data on the failed import/generate path.
supersedes.correction: The provider free callback IS invoked with NULL on that path, as the authority does; the obligation moved to the provider, whose mandatory free must tolerate NULL and whose builtin implementation now states and tests that.
That test asserted the wrong behaviour and is replaced by evp::skeymgmt::tests::a_failed_key_without_data_still_calls_the_provider_destructor_with_null.

supersedes.false_statement: M8-D1 records that EVP_SKEY_free guards `skey->keydata != NULL` and that this destructor must do the same.
supersedes.correction: The M8-D1 entry is retained as historical record, with a correction pointer to this receipt; the authority does not contain that guard.

eliminated: the false premise that the authority guards keydata before the provider free
relocated: NULL-tolerance of the mandatory provider free is now an explicit provider obligation, stated in generic_free and inherited by every provider that reuses it
retained: the provider free slot is mandatory and must not be NULL; evp_skeymgmt_freedata still dereferences skeymgmt and calls the slot (an ABI contract)

residuals.detail: The candidate now calls the provider free with NULL on the import/generate failure path, matching the authority; the builtin provider tolerates NULL and a library test pins it.

This correction does not discharge the provider-callback boundary for third-party providers: one that dereferences its keydata unconditionally would still fault on NULL, exactly as it would against the authority.
The library suite is not a Miri run; the NULL path's absence of a dereference is established by source structure and the explicit early return, not by a model checker.
